INSERT INTO _content_docs_workflows VALUES ('docs_workflows/workflows/99.adr/0001-derive-a-bodys-configuration-from-the-repo.md', 'Derive a body''s configuration from the repo', '{"type":"minimark","value":[["h1",{"id":"adr-0001-derive-a-bodys-configuration-from-the-repo"},"ADR-0001 — Derive a body''s configuration from the repo"],["h2",{"id":"context"},"Context"],["p",{},"The bodies replace workflow files that had been copied into every repo and had drifted apart. Counting the copies made them look irreconcilable — the fast-forward queue workflow existed in eight versions — but the differences between them were not eight problems. They were the integration branch name, a per-owner secret identifier, a runner label, and a group of repos that had never received a fix."],["p",{},"Each of those first values is something the repo already answers. The branch name is decided by the trigger that let the run start; the owner is on every event payload. Carried as a literal, the owner-specific identifier was wrong in several repos at once — a mismatch that resolves for nobody, silently, and surfaces only when someone dispatches the workflow."],["p",{},"A value that a caller supplies is a value the caller maintains, and a maintained value in every repo is the copy this repository exists to remove, one file smaller."],["h2",{"id":"decision"},"Decision"],["p",{},"A body reads what the repo it runs in can tell it. An input exists only for what a body genuinely cannot know — the languages an analysis should cover, the versions a matrix should span."],["p",{},"Where a body cannot read a value from the event it is triggered by, it resolves it in a job of its own and hands it to the rest through ",["code",{},"needs"],", rather than accepting it from the caller."],["h2",{"id":"consequences"},"Consequences"],["p",{},"Every calling repo carries the same stub for the same workflow, so two stubs that differ mark a real difference rather than an accident of when they were copied."],["p",{},"A repo changes its behaviour by changing itself. Creating an integration branch moves it to another branch topology and no workflow file changes anywhere — which is the property being bought, and also the surprise: nothing in the stub says the topology is a decision."],["p",{},"A whole class of error stops being possible instead of being fixed in each place it occurred."],["p",{},"The cost is paid at the body: deriving a value takes a job or a step that an input would not have needed, that job''s name becomes part of every caller''s check names, and a body is harder to exercise in isolation because it now depends on the shape of the repo around it. A repo that wants to deviate from what its own state implies cannot do so from the call site at all."],["h2",{"id":"alternatives-considered"},"Alternatives considered"],["p",{},["strong",{},"An input per value."]," Correct, conventional, and the way most reusable workflows are written. It hands each caller a value to keep in step with its own trigger — which is what the copies were doing, expressed in fewer lines."],["p",{},["strong",{},"A configuration file in the calling repo."]," The same objection, one level up, plus a second file to keep in step with the first."],["p",{},["strong",{},"One body per topology."]," This is where the eight variants came from."]],"toc":{"title":"","searchDepth":2,"depth":2,"links":[{"id":"context","depth":2,"text":"Context"},{"id":"decision","depth":2,"text":"Decision"},{"id":"consequences","depth":2,"text":"Consequences"},{"id":"alternatives-considered","depth":2,"text":"Alternatives considered"}]}}', 'A body reads the values that differ per repo out of the repo it runs in, and accepts an input only for what it cannot know.', 'md', NULL, NULL, '{"status":"accepted","date":"2026-09-01"}', NULL, '/workflows/adr/0001-derive-a-bodys-configuration-from-the-repo', '{"title":"Derive a body''s configuration from the repo","description":"A body reads the values that differ per repo out of the repo it runs in, and accepts an input only for what it cannot know."}', 'workflows/99.adr/0001-derive-a-bodys-configuration-from-the-repo', 'rg-w-4nPVvx2hi5yjLYHNinKpgdxf7m_kJip23oXoVU'); -- rg-w-4nPVvx2hi5yjLYHNinKpgdxf7m_kJip23oXoVU

A change reaches a caller only when someone merges the bump."],["p",{},"Every repo is therefore behind by however long its bump PR sits, including for a fix, and a security fix reaches the estate at the speed of review rather than at the speed of a push."],["p",{},"The trailing comment is the only thing that tells a human which version a stub is on, and nothing enforces that it stays truthful."],["p",{},"The alias defaults to off because moving a tag is a hazard where something else reads the tag list as a version list — for a published package the registry version is what resolves, and for a Terraform provider an extra unversioned tag is not valid semver at all."],["h2",{"id":"alternatives-considered"},"Alternatives considered"],["p",{},["strong",{},"A moving major tag as the default."]," One less thing for every repo to bump, at the price of the review gate above. That word is shorter than a block naming each secret, and it never needs touching again when a body grows a new requirement."],["p",{},"It also decides, once, that every secret the repository acquires from then on is visible to every body it calls — including secrets added long after anyone last read the stub, and including bodies added to the call after that."],["h2",{"id":"decision"},"Decision"],["p",{},"A stub passes exactly the secrets its body declares, one key at a time. INSERT INTO _content_docs_workflows VALUES ('docs_workflows/workflows/99.adr/0004-compose-ci-from-bodies-that-are-jobs.md', 'Compose CI from bodies that are jobs', '{"type":"minimark","value":[["h1",{"id":"adr-0004-compose-ci-from-bodies-that-are-jobs"},"ADR-0004 — Compose CI from bodies that are jobs"],["h2",{"id":"context"},"Context"],["p",{},"CI was the workflow that had drifted furthest: measured across the estate, nearly every repo''s copy was unique. Behind that were a handful of families — repos running a single gate, libraries running a typecheck-test-build set, packages running a version matrix against a database, providers running a language toolchain — and a few repos with pipelines that genuinely belong to them, carrying deploy stages and their own short-circuits."],["p",{},"Unlike the queue workflows, the differences here are not values a body can look up. Whether a repo needs a database, which toolchain it installs and what \"tested\" means for it are properties of its stack, not of its state."],["h2",{"id":"decision"},"Decision"],["p",{},"A CI body is a ",["strong",{},"job"]," that a caller composes into a pipeline it still owns, and there is one body per family rather than one body for CI."],["p",{},"Inputs on such a body say what the body cannot know — which versions a matrix spans, which paths a filter watches. They never say which parts of the body to skip."],["h2",{"id":"consequences"},"Consequences"],["p",{},"A repo keeps its own pipeline and its own graph: it decides what runs, in which order, and what a short-circuit is allowed to stand for. The bodies it calls do not need to know about each other."],["p",{},"Repos with pipelines of their own are not special cases to be worked around — they compose from the same pieces as everyone else, which is why the pieces were cut at job boundaries in the first place."],["p",{},"Adding a family means adding a body. Writing one before a second caller exists is a cost taken deliberately, and only where a named repo would otherwise start by copying the first one."],["p",{},"A caller''s pipeline is longer than a single ",["code",{},"uses:"]," line, and the composition itself — which job needs which, what gates on what — is the one thing that can still drift between repos."],["h2",{"id":"alternatives-considered"},"Alternatives considered"],["p",{},["strong",{},"One CI body with feature switches"]," — flags for running tests, for needing a database, for a coverage step. It works. It also turns every stub into a configuration file of a dozen keys, which is the drift this repository removes, reappearing one level up. It would still have left the repos with their own pipelines as special cases, and those carry the most logic."],["p",{},["strong",{},"One body per repo."]," The starting point, and what was being replaced."]],"toc":{"title":"","searchDepth":2,"depth":2,"links":[{"id":"context","depth":2,"text":"Context"},{"id":"decision","depth":2,"text":"Decision"},{"id":"consequences","depth":2,"text":"Consequences"},{"id":"alternatives-considered","depth":2,"text":"Alternatives considered"}]}}', 'A CI body is a job the caller composes into its own pipeline, never one body with switches for the parts a repo does not run.', 'md', NULL, NULL, '{"status":"accepted","date":"2026-09-01"}', NULL, '/workflows/adr/0004-compose-ci-from-bodies-that-are-jobs', '{"title":"Compose CI from bodies that are jobs","description":"A CI body is a job the caller composes into its own pipeline, never one body with switches for the parts a repo does not run."}', 'workflows/99.adr/0004-compose-ci-from-bodies-that-are-jobs', 'BYTUKGhoE40NFWDLcgZFJKEnazE5uV65NLhbKpz95mc'); -- BYTUKGhoE40NFWDLcgZFJKEnazE5uV65NLhbKpz95mc

INSERT INTO _content_docs_workflows VALUES ('docs_workflows/workflows/99.adr/0006-keep-the-composite-action-out-of-the-bodies.md', 'Keep the composite action out of the bodies', '{"type":"minimark","value":[["h1",{"id":"adr-0006-keep-the-composite-action-out-of-the-bodies"},"ADR-0006 — Keep the composite action out of the bodies"],["h2",{"id":"context"},"Context"],["p",{},"A reusable workflow is taken whole. INSERT INTO _content_docs_workflows VALUES ('docs_workflows/workflows/99.adr/0007-run-the-gate-as-one-job-with-a-step-per-check.md', 'Run the gate as one job with a step per check', '{"type":"minimark","value":[["h1",{"id":"adr-0007-run-the-gate-as-one-job-with-a-step-per-check"},"ADR-0007 — Run the gate as one job with a step per check"],["h2",{"id":"context"},"Context"],["p",{},"For the repos whose CI is a set of independent checks, the copied workflows listed those checks a second time as steps — the same commands the package manifest''s gate script already chained, kept in step by hand."],["p",{},"Deriving the list from the gate script removes that second copy, and it also decides nothing about how the tasks then run. Two shapes were available: fan them out over a matrix so each reports as its own job, or run them as steps of one job."],["p",{},"The tasks in question are short. A run for these repos is dominated by checkout and dependency install, not by the checks themselves."],["h2",{"id":"decision"},"Decision"],["p",{},"The gate body splits the repo''s gate script into its task calls, expanding a task that chains another aggregate, and runs the result as ",["strong",{},"steps of a single job"],". Each task gets its own log group and its own error line, so a failed run names the check that failed."],["h2",{"id":"consequences"},"Consequences"],["p",{},"The check list follows the repo. A repo adds a check by editing its gate script, and CI picks it up with no workflow change — which is what carries the checks that exist in only one repo, without any of them being named here."],["p",{},"A run costs one checkout and one install rather than one per task."],["p",{},"What is given up is granularity at the job level: the whole gate is one check name, so a single aspect of it cannot be required on its own, and the tasks do not run in parallel. The first task to fail ends the job, so a run reports one failure rather than all of them."],["p",{},"A task that takes arguments is left unexpanded, because running it on its own would not be the same command."],["h2",{"id":"alternatives-considered"},"Alternatives considered"],["p",{},["strong",{},"A matrix, one job per task."]," It gives each check its own name and lets any one of them be required alone. Jobs share nothing — separate runner, separate filesystem, separate dependency tree — so n tasks cost n checkouts and n installs. For a gate of short tasks that makes the run slower while occupying several runners instead of one. The trade reverses where a single task runs for minutes, which is why the bodies for the heavier stacks do use a matrix."],["p",{},["strong",{},"Running the gate script as one command."]," One step, no derivation, and a red build that does not say which check failed."]],"toc":{"title":"","searchDepth":2,"depth":2,"links":[{"id":"context","depth":2,"text":"Context"},{"id":"decision","depth":2,"text":"Decision"},{"id":"consequences","depth":2,"text":"Consequences"},{"id":"alternatives-considered","depth":2,"text":"Alternatives considered"}]}}', 'The gate body derives its task list from the repo package manifest and runs the tasks as steps of a single job rather than fanning them over a matrix.', 'md', NULL, NULL, '{"status":"accepted","date":"2026-09-01"}', NULL, '/workflows/adr/0007-run-the-gate-as-one-job-with-a-step-per-check', '{"title":"Run the gate as one job with a step per check","description":"The gate body derives its task list from the repo package manifest and runs the tasks as steps of a single job rather than fanning them over a matrix."}', 'workflows/99.adr/0007-run-the-gate-as-one-job-with-a-step-per-check', 'XM4JBXHiGAFpE0wgeL8fOfeI5QrfuA_vEMTemyaY_u0'); -- XM4JBXHiGAFpE0wgeL8fOfeI5QrfuA_vEMTemyaY_u0
INSERT INTO _content_docs_workflows VALUES ('docs_workflows/workflows/99.adr/0008-give-each-reporter-its-own-comment-thread.md', 'Give each reporter its own comment thread', '{"type":"minimark","value":[["h1",{"id":"adr-0008-give-each-reporter-its-own-comment-thread"},"ADR-0008 — Give each reporter its own comment thread"],["h2",{"id":"context"},"Context"],["p",{},"Two of the bodies write results back to a pull request: coverage, and the performance audit. Either the reporters share a marker and are no longer independent, or they are independent and there is more than one thread."],["h2",{"id":"decision"},"Decision"],["p",{},"Each reporting body owns its own sticky marker and posts under it alone. Coverage keeps the marker its action already writes; the audit posts under its own. Neither body knows the other exists."],["h2",{"id":"consequences"},"Consequences"],["p",{},"A pull request in a repo that runs both carries two comment threads instead of one. That is the cost, and it is paid on every such pull request."],["p",{},"What it buys is that either body can be adopted without the other, dropped without touching the other, and changed without a second body''s output shifting. It also removes the last reason the combined job could not be replaced: it was blocked by this coupling rather than by a missing second caller."],["p",{},"The markers now have to stay distinct by convention, since nothing enforces it — a body colliding with another''s marker would silently overwrite its report."],["h2",{"id":"alternatives-considered"},"Alternatives considered"],["p",{},["strong",{},"One shared marker, written by whichever body runs last."]," Keeps a single thread, and makes the last writer responsible for content it did not produce — a body would have to read another''s artifact to avoid erasing it. INSERT INTO _content_docs_workflows VALUES ('docs_workflows/workflows/99.adr/0009-write-a-body-before-its-second-caller.md', 'Write a body before its second caller', '{"type":"minimark","value":[["h1",{"id":"adr-0009-write-a-body-before-its-second-caller"},"ADR-0009 — Write a body before its second caller"],["h2",{"id":"context"},"Context"],["p",{},"The case for centralising a workflow is that several repos carry the same one. Where only a single repo has it, that case is absent: a body written for one caller generalises a shape nobody has met twice, and the input it takes may be the wrong seam."],["p",{},"Refusing every such body has its own cost, and it falls on a repo that does not exist yet. The next repo of a given kind starts from the only version available — a copy, taken whole, from whichever repo happened to have one. A long pipeline copied once is a second variant from its first commit, and the estate''s own history is the argument: every workflow being centralised here reached its variant count exactly that way."],["p",{},"Both failure modes are real, so the question is which repo pays: a body generalised too early, or a copy made too late."],["h2",{"id":"decision"},"Decision"],["p",{},"A body may be written for a single caller when a ",["strong",{},"named"]," repo is known to need it next — one that exists, or one a template is expected to produce. The second caller is likely to need an input that is not there, and adding it is cheap; discovering that the seam itself is wrong is not."],["p",{},"Migrating the first caller onto such a body may rename its checks, which is a branch-protection change in that repo. Accepted deliberately: it happens once, and it happens anyway during the migration."],["p",{},"The rule can be argued into anything, since any repo might one day need any workflow. The requirement that the next caller be ",["em",{},"named"]," is what keeps it a decision rather than a preference — an unnamed one is a hunch, and a hunch does not clear the bar."],["h2",{"id":"alternatives-considered"},"Alternatives considered"],["p",{},["strong",{},"Wait for the second caller, always."]," The rule as it would read without this record. It is right in the common case and wrong exactly where the second caller is a large repo whose copy would be made before anyone noticed."],["p",{},["strong",{},"Write every body speculatively."]," Removes the judgement, and fills the repository with interfaces shaped by a single example, each of which has to be broken when a real second caller arrives."]],"toc":{"title":"","searchDepth":2,"depth":2,"links":[{"id":"context","depth":2,"text":"Context"},{"id":"decision","depth":2,"text":"Decision"},{"id":"consequences","depth":2,"text":"Consequences"},{"id":"alternatives-considered","depth":2,"text":"Alternatives considered"}]}}', 'A body may be written for a single caller when a specific repo is known to need it next, and the reasoning is recorded with the body.', 'md', NULL, NULL, '{"status":"accepted","date":"2026-09-01"}', NULL, '/workflows/adr/0009-write-a-body-before-its-second-caller', '{"title":"Write a body before its second caller","description":"A body may be written for a single caller when a specific repo is known to need it next, and the reasoning is recorded with the body."}', 'workflows/99.adr/0009-write-a-body-before-its-second-caller', 'S8vRgfxmlypC7P2UONNLFtNvQ_FRMk60zQZlKLU5Qwc'); -- S8vRgfxmlypC7P2UONNLFtNvQ_FRMk60zQZlKLU5Qwc

Each task gets its own log group and its own error line, so a failed run names the check that failed."],["h2",{"id":"consequences"},"Consequences"],["p",{},"The check list follows the repo. A repo adds a check by editing its gate script, and CI picks it up with no workflow change — which is what carries the checks that exist in only one repo, without any of them being named here."],["p",{},"A run costs one checkout and one install rather than one per task."],["p",{},"What is given up is granularity at the job level: the whole gate is one check name, so a single aspect of it cannot be required on its own, and the tasks do not run in parallel. The first task to fail ends the job, so a run reports one failure rather than all of them."],["p",{},"A task that takes arguments is left unexpanded, because running it on its own would not be the same command."],["h2",{"id":"alternatives-considered"},"Alternatives considered"],["p",{},["strong",{},"A matrix, one job per task."]," It gives each check its own name and lets any one of them be required alone. Jobs share nothing — separate runner, separate filesystem, separate dependency tree — so n tasks cost n checkouts and n installs. For a gate of short tasks that makes the run slower while occupying several runners instead of one. The trade reverses where a single task runs for minutes, which is why the bodies for the heavier stacks do use a matrix."],["p",{},["strong",{},"Running the gate script as one command."]," One step, no derivation, and a red build that does not say which check failed."]],"toc":{"title":"","searchDepth":2,"depth":2,"links":[{"id":"context","depth":2,"text":"Context"},{"id":"decision","depth":2,"text":"Decision"},{"id":"consequences","depth":2,"text":"Consequences"},{"id":"alternatives-considered","depth":2,"text":"Alternatives considered"}]}}', 'The gate body derives its task list from the repo package manifest and runs the tasks as steps of a single job rather than fanning them over a matrix.', 'md', NULL, NULL, '{"status":"accepted","date":"2026-09-01"}', NULL, '/workflows/v0.7.0/adr/0007-run-the-gate-as-one-job-with-a-step-per-check', '{"title":"Run the gate as one job with a step per check","description":"The gate body derives its task list from the repo package manifest and runs the tasks as steps of a single job rather than fanning them over a matrix."}', 'workflows/v0.7.0/99.adr/0007-run-the-gate-as-one-job-with-a-step-per-check', 't-09cWvwua-z-Wc03uksue16mi1-9JVkjzchvL0gLQE'); -- t-09cWvwua-z-Wc03uksue16mi1-9JVkjzchvL0gLQE

The repository they were derived from had collected both into a single comment, and said why — a second reporting job beside it would open a second thread, and a pull request carrying a thread per metric is one nobody reads."],["p",{},"That reasoning holds for a pipeline written in one file. It does not survive being split into bodies that repos compose independently. A repo calling the coverage body alongside the combined job would get the second thread anyway, because the two know nothing about each other; and coupling them so they do not would mean one body reading another''s output, which is the shape the split was meant to avoid. Either the reporters share a marker and are no longer independent, or they are independent and there is more than one thread."],["h2",{"id":"decision"},"Decision"],["p",{},"Each reporting body owns its own sticky marker and posts under it alone. Coverage keeps the marker its action already writes; the audit posts under its own. Neither body knows the other exists."],["h2",{"id":"consequences"},"Consequences"],["p",{},"A pull request in a repo that runs both carries two comment threads instead of one. That is the cost, and it is paid on every such pull request."],["p",{},"What it buys is that either body can be adopted without the other, dropped without touching the other, and changed without a second body''s output shifting. It also removes the last reason the combined job could not be replaced: it was blocked by this coupling rather than by a missing second caller."],["p",{},"The markers now have to stay distinct by convention, since nothing enforces it — a body colliding with another''s marker would silently overwrite its report."],["h2",{"id":"alternatives-considered"},"Alternatives considered"],["p",{},["strong",{},"One shared marker, written by whichever body runs last."]," Keeps a single thread, and makes the last writer responsible for content it did not produce — a body would have to read another''s artifact to avoid erasing it. The coupling that was being removed, reintroduced at the comment level."],["p",{},["strong",{},"One reporting body aggregating the others."]," A single thread again, at the price of a body that must know every reporter that exists, and must be extended before any new one can report anything."]],"toc":{"title":"","searchDepth":2,"depth":2,"links":[{"id":"context","depth":2,"text":"Context"},{"id":"decision","depth":2,"text":"Decision"},{"id":"consequences","depth":2,"text":"Consequences"},{"id":"alternatives-considered","depth":2,"text":"Alternatives considered"}]}}', 'A body that reports to a pull request owns its own sticky marker, rather than several reporters sharing one comment.', 'md', NULL, NULL, '{"status":"accepted","date":"2026-09-01"}', NULL, '/workflows/v0.7.0/adr/0008-give-each-reporter-its-own-comment-thread', '{"title":"Give each reporter its own comment thread","description":"A body that reports to a pull request owns its own sticky marker, rather than several reporters sharing one comment."}', 'workflows/v0.7.0/99.adr/0008-give-each-reporter-its-own-comment-thread', 'YGJZIajkVGSblpQyl4Kt3jOJ9dgt1qj21S6e_OdJsmY'); -- YGJZIajkVGSblpQyl4Kt3jOJ9dgt1qj21S6e_OdJsmY
INSERT INTO _content_docs_workflows_v0_7_0 VALUES ('docs_workflows_v0_7_0/workflows/v0.7.0/99.adr/0009-write-a-body-before-its-second-caller.md', 'Write a body before its second caller', '{"type":"minimark","value":[["h1",{"id":"adr-0009-write-a-body-before-its-second-caller"},"ADR-0009 — Write a body before its second caller"],["h2",{"id":"context"},"Context"],["p",{},"The case for centralising a workflow is that several repos carry the same one. Where only a single repo has it, that case is absent: a body written for one caller generalises a shape nobody has met twice, and the input it takes may be the wrong seam."],["p",{},"Refusing every such body has its own cost, and it falls on a repo that does not exist yet. The next repo of a given kind starts from the only version available — a copy, taken whole, from whichever repo happened to have one. A long pipeline copied once is a second variant from its first commit, and the estate''s own history is the argument: every workflow being centralised here reached its variant count exactly that way."],["p",{},"Both failure modes are real, so the question is which repo pays: a body generalised too early, or a copy made too late."],["h2",{"id":"decision"},"Decision"],["p",{},"A body may be written for a single caller when a ",["strong",{},"named"]," repo is known to need it next — one that exists, or one a template is expected to produce. The reasoning goes in the body''s own header, naming that repo, so a later reader can tell a considered exception from an oversight."],["p",{},"Where no such repo can be named, one instance is not a pattern and no body is written."],["h2",{"id":"consequences"},"Consequences"],["p",{},"A body written this way has had its interface guessed once rather than observed twice. The second caller is likely to need an input that is not there, and adding it is cheap; discovering that the seam itself is wrong is not."],["p",{},"Migrating the first caller onto such a body may rename its checks, which is a branch-protection change in that repo. Accepted deliberately: it happens once, and it happens anyway during the migration."],["p",{},"The rule can be argued into anything, since any repo might one day need any workflow. The requirement that the next caller be ",["em",{},"named"]," is what keeps it a decision rather than a preference — an unnamed one is a hunch, and a hunch does not clear the bar."],["h2",{"id":"alternatives-considered"},"Alternatives considered"],["p",{},["strong",{},"Wait for the second caller, always."]," The rule as it would read without this record. It is right in the common case and wrong exactly where the second caller is a large repo whose copy would be made before anyone noticed."],["p",{},["strong",{},"Write every body speculatively."]," Removes the judgement, and fills the repository with interfaces shaped by a single example, each of which has to be broken when a real second caller arrives."]],"toc":{"title":"","searchDepth":2,"depth":2,"links":[{"id":"context","depth":2,"text":"Context"},{"id":"decision","depth":2,"text":"Decision"},{"id":"consequences","depth":2,"text":"Consequences"},{"id":"alternatives-considered","depth":2,"text":"Alternatives considered"}]}}', 'A body may be written for a single caller when a specific repo is known to need it next, and the reasoning is recorded with the body.', 'md', NULL, NULL, '{"status":"accepted","date":"2026-09-01"}', NULL, '/workflows/v0.7.0/adr/0009-write-a-body-before-its-second-caller', '{"title":"Write a body before its second caller","description":"A body may be written for a single caller when a specific repo is known to need it next, and the reasoning is recorded with the body."}', 'workflows/v0.7.0/99.adr/0009-write-a-body-before-its-second-caller', 'yK0uKfsrv0aTWuGVByNVx1YUSy8_DbuEd6V2kcrPmiY'); -- yK0uKfsrv0aTWuGVByNVx1YUSy8_DbuEd6V2kcrPmiY
